name: KYS (Bhat et al. ECCV 2020) - propagation of scene state, including neighbours, by dense correspondence
bibliography: Goutam Bhat, Martin Danelljan, Luc Van Gool, Radu Timofte. Know Your Surroundings: Exploiting Scene Information for Object Tracking. ECCV 2020 (LNCS); preprint arXiv:2003.11014 - same study. Code: released in the PyTracking library (https://github.com/visionml/pytracking, tracker 'kys') [uncertain - the arXiv text says code will be released; release in PyTracking is from memory, not verified here].
full_text_checked: Short screening: arXiv full text (ar5iv HTML) - method, training, Table 1 ablation, main results and qualitative failure case. Code and supplementary not inspected. Parts of the HTML text are garbled (FPS value, number of benchmarks).
task_and_output: Single-object tracking; output a fused target confidence map (DiMP appearance score combined with propagated scene states), box via DiMP/IoU-Net refinement.
data_and_independent_videos: Trained end-to-end on TrackingNet, LaSOT, GOT-10k train sequences (1500 sub-sequences of length 50 per epoch, 40 epochs); evaluated on unseen test sets VOT2018, GOT-10k, TrackingNet, OTB-100, NFS; ablations on NFS + OTB-100 (200 videos).
target_size_and_input_resolution: Search crop 5x5 target area resized to 288x288; ResNet-50 block-4 features, stride 16, 18x18 grid.
frame_rate_and_camera_motion: Benchmark frame rates (NFS 30-fps version); correspondence limited to 9 cells displacement; camera motion not modeled separately.
detector_and_exemplar: No detector; first-frame box; DiMP online target model plus states initialised from the first-frame label map.
trainable_nodes_and_loss: Trained: state initialiser, correspondence network over a 4D cost volume, ConvGRU state update, fusion predictor; backbone frozen (GPU memory). Losses: least squares to Gaussian label on fused score, auxiliary raw-score loss, BCE state-classification losses (alpha = beta = 0.1). Random distractor peaks added to appearance scores during training.
controls_seeds_splits: Ablation on NFS + OTB-100 (Table 1): appearance-only DiMP-50, no state propagation, no reliability, no appearance model. Single runs; no seeds or intervals.
metrics_and_numbers: arXiv 2003.11014, Table 1 (NFS+OTB-100, AUC / OP0.5): full 66.4 / 83.5; only appearance (DiMP-50) 65.1 / 81.9; no state propagation 64.9 / 81.2; no reliability 66.1 / 82.9; no appearance model 49.2 / 60.1. VOT2018 EAO 0.462 vs DiMP-50 0.440; GOT-10k AO 63.6 vs 61.1; TrackingNet AUC 74.0 (equal to DiMP-50); NFS AUC 63.5. Speed about 20 FPS on RTX 2080 [uncertain, garbled text].
tested_conditions: Unseen videos: yes. Target absence: not reported (state update skipped if fused peak < 0.05). Similar distractors: motivation and qualitative figures only; no quantitative distractor subset. Occlusion: qualitative failure case (occluder taken over). Night/low light: not reported. Sequential operation on own predictions: yes (online, states updated from own outputs).
mechanism_summary: Published: an 8-dim learned state vector at each of 18x18 locations encodes target/background/distractor cues; states are transported to the next frame by a soft dense correspondence computed from a local cost volume of backbone features; correspondence entropy gives reliability; a predictor fuses propagated states with the DiMP score; a ConvGRU updates states. Gain over appearance-only DiMP is +1.3 AUC on the 200-video ablation set; without propagation the extra modules are worse than DiMP alone. Proposed (ours): treat FlyVis cell-type activity in the moving crop as the correspondence feature and carry per-location target/neighbour labels between frames with the crop shift compensated.
transfer_limits: Requires dense correspondence between consecutive search crops; our crop moves and rescales with the prediction, and during a loss episode there is no verified target frame - states would be propagated from the last observation over up to 30 frames, accumulating drift (the paper itself reports state leakage into a slowly crossing occluder). FlyVis provides 34 cell-type motion/brightness responses on 721 grey hexals - correspondence from such features on a ~9x12-step target is unverified. The gain is small (+1.3 AUC) even with ResNet features. No MOT association link.
research_questions_addressed: 5.1: design analogy - neighbour identity carried by scene state rather than by the appearance map; refusal not addressed. 5.2: design analogy for representing neighbours explicitly per location over time; caution about leakage. 5.3: not addressed (backbone frozen). 5.4: not addressed.
candidate_node_change: Not recommended now. If pursued: node = state transfer of the FlyVis readout (per-hexal label map carried by FlyVis-derived optical flow between crops). Controls: label map carried by the Kalman crop shift only (no FlyVis) and by stock FlyVis; minimal check on saved train26 episodes whether carried labels keep the old target peak versus neighbour peaks; stop if not better than the Kalman-shift carry with CI lower bound > 0.
strongest_objection: Small effect on RGB features (+1.3 AUC) and dependence on reliable dense correspondence that our tiny grey FlyVis crops and loss episodes cannot provide; equivalent per-candidate identity carrying was already tried and failed (z13_candidate_identity_v1).
evidence_strength: Peer-reviewed (ECCV 2020); single runs; ablation on 200 videos only; code availability not verified here. Moderate for the claim on RGB benchmarks, weak for our setting.
where_distinction_is_made: In the representation/memory: learned per-location state vectors (trained with BCE state-classification losses) mark target vs background vs distractor; the final decision fuses them with the appearance map, so a high appearance maximum on a location whose carried state says 'distractor' is down-weighted. Presence / outside area / insufficient data are not separated (only a 0.05 peak threshold for skipping updates).
feature_dependence: Correspondence is computed from ResNet-50 block-4 features (1024 channels); depends on rich appearance features. No evidence for small motion/brightness features.
difference_from_tried: Difference from our observation memory (z13_observed_memory_v1) and query memory (z13_query_memory_v1): KYS stores dense spatial labels of the whole neighbourhood and transports them by correspondence, not exemplar appearance vectors. Difference from framewise candidate identity (z13_candidate_identity_v1, completed_negative): KYS is dense and learned, our version tracked discrete peaks; the principle (keep track of what not to track over frames) is the same and was already tested negatively in its discrete form.
memory_write_policy: Not applicable as a memory bank; states updated every frame by ConvGRU unless the fused peak < 0.05.
distractor_representation: Explicit but dense and learned: per-location state vectors with a distractor-related classification loss.
refusal_evidence_horizon: Not applicable (no refusal); states accumulate over frames.
loss_on_applied_decision: On the fused score map (intermediate to the box), not on an applied association decision.
no_fly_control_equivalent: Not applicable as a new control; if pursued, label map carried by the Kalman/crop shift alone.
temporal_information_availability: Causal: current and previous frame only (states summarise the past); no added latency.
depth_level: Short screening. Loses: small published gain, needs dense correspondence from rich features, and its discrete analogue in our project (candidate identity carrying) already failed; should not move to full analysis. KeepTrack (N01) is the same authors' later and stronger version of the idea.
